title: Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number
main_claim: There is a simply connected closed Kähler manifold M = X×Y of real dimension 2N+4 (N≥704; dim 1412 for N=704) and a Hamiltonian H, all of whose fixed points are nondegenerate and contractible, with #Fix = SM(M) − 16 (318952 vs 318968). Here X is CP^N blown up along the bielliptic surface S_2 and along S_3×CP^1×CP^1, and Y is CP^1×CP^1 blown up at four points, which carries a Hamiltonian half-turn involution.
sibling_notes: The construction matches the dim-22 companion: the same S_2/S_3 bielliptic surfaces, the same Y half-turn, and the same involution proposition and handle appendix. In this paper the second center gets two extra CP^1 factors, which produce the torsion profile (1,3,4,…,4,3,1) and a gap of 16 that does not depend on N. My recomputation agrees with the sibling's findings for the shared lemmas.
